---
title: "How the pipeline works"
---

`omero-screen <plate_id>` runs `plate_loop()`, which fetches the plate from
OMERO, segments every image, measures every cell and writes the results back to
the plate. This page describes each stage and the configuration that controls
it. Every command-line option is listed in the
[CLI reference](../reference/cli/omero_screen.qmd).

## The stages

::: {.fig-card}
![Starting from a plate ID, the pipeline parses experimental metadata, builds per-channel flatfield masks, then iterates over every non-empty well. Each image is segmented with Cellpose, features are extracted with `regionprops`, and results are written back to OMERO as CSV attachments. Cell-cycle assignment and optional classification run once all wells are done.](../assets/analysis-loop.svg){#fig-loop width=85%}
:::

1. **Metadata parsing.** The experimental layout (well positions, cell lines,
   conditions, channel names) is read from an Excel file attached to the plate.
   It is then converted to OMERO map annotations and the Excel file is removed.
2. **Flatfield correction.** Per-channel illumination masks are built from a
   random sample of 100 images across the plate. The masks are stored in a
   dedicated OMERO dataset, so later runs skip this step.
3. **Well and image loop.** For each non-empty well and each image in it:
   - the raw pixels are downloaded and divided by the flatfield mask;
   - Cellpose segments nuclei (DAPI/Hoechst channel) and cells (cytoplasm
     channel);
   - objects touching the border are removed, and the cytoplasm mask is derived
     as cell minus nucleus;
   - `skimage.measure.regionprops_table` measures the nucleus, cell and
     cytoplasm regions (see [Extracted features](#extracted-features));
   - the well's results are attached to OMERO as an intermediate CSV, so a
     crashed run can resume.
4. **Cell-cycle analysis.** If the plate has an EdU channel, integrated DAPI
   intensity and EdU signal are normalised per cell line and each nucleus is
   assigned to sub-G1, G1, S, G2/M or polyploid.
5. **Save results.** Plate-level CSVs and QC figures are attached to the plate;
   the intermediate per-well files are deleted.

Tiled plates and timelapses are better served by
[stitched mode](stitching.qmd), which segments the whole well as one canvas.

## Re-running a plate

A re-run reuses the segmentation masks already stored in OMERO and only
recomputes the measurements. Add `--delete` to discard the stored masks and
segment from scratch, for example after changing a model or a
[segmentation profile](#per-channel-segmentation-profiles).

## Configuration file

Models, features and segmentation profiles come from a JSON configuration. The
built-in defaults live in `src/data/omero_screen_config.json`. To use your own,
point `OMERO_SCREEN_CONFIG` at a JSON file, or pass `--config PATH`, which takes
precedence over the variable. A path that does not exist is an error; the
pipeline does not fall back to the defaults.

The file may contain any of three blocks: `MODEL_DICT`, `FEATURELIST` and
`CHANNEL_SEG_PROFILES`.

## Extracted features

`FEATURELIST` declares which `regionprops` properties are measured, split into
two groups:

```json
{
  "FEATURELIST": {
    "intensity":  ["intensity_mean", "intensity_max", "intensity_min", "intensity_std"],
    "morphology": ["area", "solidity", "eccentricity", "extent", "perimeter",
                   "area_convex", "axis_major_length", "axis_minor_length",
                   "equivalent_diameter_area"]
  }
}
```

- **Intensity** features read the pixel data, so they are measured per channel
  and named `{feature}_{channel}_{segment}`.
- **Morphology** features read only the label mask, so they are the same on
  every channel. They are measured once per segment, on the channel that
  produced the mask, and named `{feature}_{segment}`.
- `label` and `centroid` are identity columns and are always added; don't list
  them.

Feature names must be valid `skimage.measure.regionprops` properties. `area` and
`intensity_mean` are required, because the integrated-intensity column is
computed from them, and their presence is checked when the configuration loads.
A flat list (the older format) is still accepted and split into the two groups
automatically.

The default set is deliberately small. A richer, cell-state-oriented set ships
as `src/data/omero_screen_config_full.json`:

```bash
uv run omero-screen <plate_id> --config src/data/omero_screen_config_full.json
```

## Per-channel segmentation profiles

Cellpose's default thresholds suit fixed-cell stains such as DAPI and Hoechst,
which are bright and even. They miss cells on live-cell markers with variable
brightness, such as H2B-RFP, or heterogeneous expression, such as Tubulin-GFP.
`CHANNEL_SEG_PROFILES` applies its own preprocessing and Cellpose parameters
when a channel of that name is segmented. The built-in profiles are:

```json
{
  "CHANNEL_SEG_PROFILES": {
    "h2b_rfp": {"gamma": 0.5, "cellprob_threshold": -2.0},
    "tub_gfp": {"gamma": 0.5, "cellprob_threshold": -2.0, "flow_threshold": 0.6}
  }
}
```

Channel names are matched case-insensitively. Three keys are supported:

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `gamma` | Dynamic-range compression after percentile rescaling, before Cellpose. Values below 1 lift dim nuclei in frames that also contain bright ones. |
| `cellprob_threshold` | Passed to Cellpose's `eval()`. Lower it (e.g. `-2`) to accept less confident detections. |
| `flow_threshold` | Passed to Cellpose's `eval()`. Helps cell segmentation when the Tubulin signal is faint at the cell edge. |

Profiles in your configuration file are **merged** with the built-in ones: an
entry replaces the built-in profile of the same name, and the others stay in
place. Channels without a profile use the default Cellpose parameters, so
fixed-cell plates are unaffected.
